body:
It seems I glossed over the important part of the PR description.

I don't love the idea of maintaining this list of exceptions, to be honest, and I don't really use SCU builds myself either, but I can see how it would be beneficial to those who do.

How does it usually present itself when you do run into problems with this stuff? Is it mostly straight-forward compilation errors about conflicting identifiers and such, or can it be more cryptic linker errors and stuff as well?

> I don't love the idea of maintaining this list of exceptions, to be honest, and I don't really use SCU builds myself either, but I can see how it would be beneficial to those who do.

We also use SCU builds and I think Jolt has been configured to use it too. In our case, it does not create a single compilation unit but several per project. `Character` and `Ragdoll` must have ended up in different compilation units. In any case I fixed the problem in https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/commit/d497df2b9b0fa9aaf41295e1406079c23148232d so if you take that, there should not be a need to maintain an exclusion list.

> How does it usually present itself when you do run into problems with this stuff? Is it mostly straight-forward compilation errors about conflicting identifiers and such, or can it be more cryptic linker errors and stuff as well?

The main issue I see with SCU builds is that people using those builds forget to include files that are needed in non-SCU builds. This is a constant battle because nobody uses non-SCU builds because they're much slower. The only issues I've seen with SCU builds is that two cpp files end up defining the same function/variable. The error is very clear in that case. I don't think I've ever seen linking errors.
Mihe, yes we can use globbing. Will reply more when home the weekend. 👍

> How does it usually present itself when you do run into problems with this stuff? Is it mostly straight-forward compilation errors about conflicting identifiers and such, or can it be more cryptic linker errors and stuff as well?

Yeah it's normally pretty obvious. Conflicting identifiers, or a file not being included in the build. If you aren't sure and have a problem just ask on rocketchat. Most other non-thirdparty Godot code is already SCU accelerated.

We've been using SCU builds already for a couple of years now so we are fairly confident in quickly identifying any problems, and additionally we use a SCU build in one of the CI builds, so it's not common to accidentally merge something that breaks the SCU build.

> The main issue I see with SCU builds is that people using those builds forget to include files that are needed in non-SCU builds. This is a constant battle because nobody uses non-SCU builds because they're much slower. 

In Godot many regular contributors use SCU builds (as they are faster for development), but the CI is mainly non-SCU builds (except one I believe) which ensures that all includes are correct before passing CI, and a PR doesn't break SCU build. Final builds are also non-SCU, so we use them mainly for development.

I've now added folder globbing which should mean in most cases there is no maintenance needed by the Jolt contributors. That might make it easier to do a bit more of `thirdparty` but I'll wait until this PR is done first.

> ### Disables
> 
> The reason the resource `SCsub` files weren't working is because the SCU recognises `*.cpp` in a folder but doesn't recognise the pattern of `if not env["disable_physics_2d"]:`. In order to get around this it now detects if there are no disables, and if not, `add_source_files "*.cpp"`.
> 
> This means that in SCU builds these folders will be accelerated _unless_ you disable these parts from the build via scons etc, in which case they revert to the old build method.

I'm not fond of this pattern, as it makes SCU specific quirks seep into the rest of the buildsystem.

I really liked that up until now SCU was super well self-contained and almost no modifications to the individual SCsub were needed. I'd prefer if we could keep it this way somehow.

Notably adding code differently based on whether or not SCU is enabled is not only awkward, but could lead to bugs. Where we were carefully listing which files to build, we're now globbing, potentially building files we don't want to include (e.g. for Jolt when the hardcoded list of files to build is replaced by a globbing pattern).

It's a difficult one to get around - SCU by nature relies on globbing.

If the `SCsub` is simple and just adds all the files in the folder, it works well, because the globbing in `scu_builders` matches the globbing in `SCsub`.

If the build system wants to specify files individually in `SCsub`, or exclude files depending on conditions, then things get more difficult. At present we either put in lines like the above, or they don't get accelerated. Pick your poison.. :slightly_smiling_face: 

The other option of course is to build these manually as SCU globs in regular builds, then you get the best of both worlds. We can do this if preferred. (i.e. Write the list of files to compile in a `cpp` file, rather than `SCsub`.)
